newsitem.title: JAPAN: Daihatsu to export new recreation vehicles.
newsitem.headline: Daihatsu to export new recreation vehicles.

text.p: Daihatsu Motor Co Ltd will start exporting its Pyzar compact minivan-type recreational vehicle in late December, a Daihatsu spokesman told Reuters on Monday.

Daihatsu, owned 33.4 percent by Toyota Motor Corp, will export the Pyzars to Europe, Australia, Latin America and Southeast Asia, with a total monthly rate of 800 units. The exports to the Europe will start next January, he said.
Domestic sales of Daihatsu cars rose a steep 305.4 percent in November to 3,677 due to strong demand for the Pyzar model.
Daihatsu, Japan's second biggest minicar maker, will also start exporting its Move 660cc minivan-type recreational vehicle to similar areas from next February, the spokesman said.
Daihatsu will export a total of 1,000 Moves per month. The model for overseas sales will be equipped with 850cc engine, the spokesman said.
Daihatsu's domestic sales of its 660cc minivehicles rose 15.6 percent from a year earlier to 377,446 in the January-to-October period.
